**[Section 4 --- Confirmation Standards and Cram-Down Provisions]{.underline}**

Because not all impaired classes have accepted the Plan, confirmation of the Plan cannot be obtained solely under Section 1129(a) of the Bankruptcy Code. Accordingly, the Debtor will seek confirmation of the Plan under the \"cram-down\" provisions of Section 1129(b) of the Bankruptcy Code with respect to Class 3 (Second Lien Secured Claims) and Class 5 (Subordinated Claims / Penalty Claims).

**Section 1129(a)(10) Requirement.** As a threshold condition to cram-down under Section 1129(b), Section 1129(a)(10) of the Bankruptcy Code requires that at least one class of impaired claims must have accepted the Plan, \"determined without including any acceptance of the plan by any insider.\" As set forth in Section 3 above, both Class 2 and Class 4 have voted to accept the Plan. The insider analysis applicable to these classes is set forth in Section 5 below.

**Section 1129(b) Standard.** Under Section 1129(b), the Plan must be \"fair and equitable\" and must not \"discriminate unfairly\" against any dissenting impaired class. With respect to Class 3 (Second Lien Secured Claims), the Plan provides the indubitable equivalent of such claims or, alternatively, the holders retain their liens securing allowed claims and will receive deferred cash payments totaling at least the allowed amount of their claims as of the Effective Date. With respect to Class 5 (Subordinated Claims / Penalty Claims), the Plan respects the absolute priority rule, as subordinated creditors receive distributions only after all allowed Class 4 general unsecured claims are paid in full, consistent with the contractual and statutory subordination applicable to such claims.

The Debtor reserves all rights to modify the Plan, amend or supplement the Disclosure Statement, or seek any other relief necessary to obtain confirmation of the Plan, in each case to the extent permitted by the Bankruptcy Code and the Bankruptcy Rules.

**[Section 5 --- Identification of Insiders and Insider Claims]{.underline}**

Under Section 101(31) of the Bankruptcy Code, \"insiders\" of a corporate debtor include, but are not limited to, directors, officers, persons in control, partnerships in which the debtor is a general partner, general partners of the debtor, and relatives of a general partner, director, officer, or person in control of the debtor. An affiliate of the debtor, or an insider of an affiliate as if such affiliate were the debtor, is also an insider. The identification of insiders and any insider claims is relevant to the Section 1129(a)(10) analysis, as that section requires that at least one impaired class accept the Plan \"determined without including any acceptance of the plan by any insider.\"

**Insider Individuals. Marcus Ainsworth**, Chief Executive Officer of Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc., is an insider of the Debtor within the meaning of Section 101(31). Mr. Ainsworth does not hold any claim in any class under the Plan. He is not a holder in Class 2 or Class 4. Mr. Ainsworth did not submit a ballot and did not vote on the Plan.

**Priya Dasgupta**, Chief Financial Officer of Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc., is an insider of the Debtor within the meaning of Section 101(31). Ms. Dasgupta does not hold any claim in any class under the Plan. She is not a holder in Class 2 or Class 4. Ms. Dasgupta did not submit a ballot and did not vote on the Plan.

**Insider Entities. Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC** is a Delaware limited liability company that is wholly owned by Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. As a subsidiary and affiliate of the Debtor, Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC is an insider of the Debtor within the meaning of Section 101(31) of the Bankruptcy Code. Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC holds a general unsecured claim in **Class 4** in the amount of **\$320,000.00** (Claim No. 203, filed on May 14, 2024). Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC **submitted a ballot voting to accept the Plan**.

No other insider claims have been identified in any voting class under the Plan.

**Relevance to Section 1129(a)(10) --- Insider Exclusion Analysis**

Section 1129(a)(10) requires that at least one impaired class of claims accept the Plan, \"determined without including any acceptance of the plan by any insider.\" Because Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC is an insider of the Debtor and voted to accept the Plan in Class 4, its acceptance must be excluded for purposes of testing whether Class 4\'s acceptance satisfies the requirements of Section 1129(a)(10).

**Class 2 Insider Analysis.** No insider of the Debtor holds any claim in Class 2. Accordingly, the Class 2 acceptance results (90.00% by number of ballots; 94.97% by dollar amount of claims) are unaffected by the insider exclusion requirement of Section 1129(a)(10). Class 2 independently satisfies Section 1129(a)(10).

**Class 4 Insider Analysis.** Excluding the ballot of Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC (\$320,000.00 accepting), the adjusted Class 4 voting results are as follows:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Category**                            **Ballots**             **Dollar Amount**
  --------------------------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Accepting (excluding insider)           208                     \$23,998,400.00

  Rejecting                               71                      \$9,081,600.00

  **Total Counted (excluding insider)**   **279**                 **\$33,080,000.00**
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Acceptance by number of ballots (excluding insider): 208 of 279 = 74.55% (still exceeds the greater-than-50% threshold). Acceptance by dollar amount (excluding insider): \$23,998,400.00 of \$33,080,000.00 = 72.54% (still exceeds the two-thirds (66⅔%) threshold).

**Class 4 still accepts the Plan even when the insider vote of Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC is excluded.** Therefore, both Class 2 and Class 4 satisfy the requirements of Section 1129(a)(10), and the Debtor may proceed with cram-down confirmation under Section 1129(b) with respect to the dissenting impaired classes.

**[Section 6 --- Key Plan Milestones and Conditions to Effectiveness]{.underline}**

**Confirmation Hearing. The Confirmation Hearing on the Plan is scheduled for December 16, 2024, before the Honorable Judge Karen B. Oswald, United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, located at 824 North Market Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. Objections to confirmation of the Plan must be filed in accordance with the procedures established by the Court.**

**Conditions Precedent to the Effective Date.** The Plan shall not become effective unless and until all of the following conditions precedent have been satisfied or waived in accordance with the Plan:

> \(a\) the Confirmation Order shall have been entered by the Bankruptcy Court, which Confirmation Order shall be a Final Order (as defined in the Plan);
>
> \(b\) all documents and agreements necessary to implement the Plan shall have been executed and delivered, including the new first lien credit agreement governing the new first lien term loans in the aggregate principal amount of \$225,000,000;
>
> \(c\) all governmental and regulatory approvals necessary to consummate the Plan shall have been obtained;
>
> \(d\) all allowed administrative expense claims and professional fee claims shall have been paid or provision shall have been made for such payment in accordance with the Plan; and
>
> \(e\) all other conditions specified in Article IX of the Plan shall have been satisfied or waived.

**Projected Effective Date.** The Debtor anticipates that the Effective Date of the Plan will occur on or before January 31, 2025, or such later date as the Debtor may determine in its sole discretion, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the foregoing conditions.

**Retention of Jurisdiction.** Pursuant to Article XI of the Plan, the Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction over all matters arising out of or related to the Chapter 11 Case and the Plan, including, without limitation, the resolution of disputed claims, the enforcement and interpretation of the Plan and the Confirmation Order, and any modifications to the Plan to the extent permitted by the Bankruptcy Code.

**[Section 7 --- Key Risk Factors]{.underline}**

The Plan is subject to certain risks, and no assurance can be given that the Plan will be confirmed by the Bankruptcy Court or that the conditions to the Effective Date will be satisfied. Among the risk factors that may affect confirmation and consummation of the Plan are the following:

> • **Cram-Down Litigation.** Because Classes 3 and 5 have rejected the Plan, the Debtor must satisfy the cram-down requirements of Section 1129(b), including establishing that the Plan is \"fair and equitable\" and does not \"discriminate unfairly\" with respect to those dissenting classes. There can be no assurance that the Bankruptcy Court will find the Plan satisfies these requirements.
>
> • **Pending Claims Objections.** Seven (7) provisional ballots in Class 4, representing \$2,630,000.00 in claims subject to pending objections, have been included in the Class 4 voting tabulation. The resolution of these claims objections may affect the final Class 4 voting results.
>
> • **Section 1126(e) Designation Order.** The order designating and excluding the vote of Garnet Creek Capital Fund II, LP (\$11,300,000.00 in Class 2 claims) (Dkt. No. 461) may be subject to appeal or reconsideration.
>
> • **Ballot Irregularities.** Potential challenges may arise with respect to ballot irregularities, including the Evergreen Institutional Credit Fund ballot (Claim No. 8, \$15,600,000.00 in Class 2), which was counted as an acceptance despite an irregularity in ballot completion, and the Ridgeview Opportunity Fund LP late ballot (\$6,200,000.00 in Class 3), which was excluded for untimeliness.
>
> • **Claims Reconciliation.** Ongoing claims reconciliation may result in adjustments to the total allowed claims universe for any class, which could affect estimated recoveries and distribution amounts.

"""Recalculate all formulas in a .xlsx via LibreOffice headless (ground truth).

Usage: python recalc_libreoffice.py input.xlsx output.xlsx

Drives soffice with --calc to open the workbook, recalculate, and save.
The conversion mode triggers a full recalc.
"""
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
from soffice import run_soffice


def recalc(input_path: Path, output_path: Path):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td_path = Path(td)
        # Convert via xlsx → xlsx triggers a recalc on save
        result = run_soffice([
            "--calc",
            "--convert-to", "xlsx",
            "--outdir", str(td_path),
            str(input_path),
        ])
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"soffice failed: {result.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)

        produced = list(td_path.glob("*.xlsx"))
        if not produced:
            print("ERROR: no xlsx produced by soffice", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.move(str(produced[0]), str(output_path))
    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: recalc_libreoffice.py <input.xlsx> <output.xlsx>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    recalc(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))
"""Scan a .xlsx for formula error values.

Usage: python scan_errors.py file.xlsx > errors.json

Reports every cell whose value matches one of the seven Excel error codes:
  #REF!  #DIV/0!  #VALUE!  #NAME?  #NULL!  #NUM!  #N/A

Run after every recalc. Don't ship a workbook with errors.
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl


ERROR_VALUES = {"#REF!", "#DIV/0!", "#VALUE!", "#NAME?", "#NULL!", "#NUM!", "#N/A"}


def scan(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(str(path), data_only=False)
    hits = []
    for sheet_name in wb.sheetnames:
        ws = wb[sheet_name]
        for row in ws.iter_rows():
            for cell in row:
                v = cell.value
                if isinstance(v, str) and v in ERROR_VALUES:
                    hits.append({"sheet": sheet_name, "address": cell.coordinate, "value": v})
    return hits

content.text:
I built `ballot-tabulation-summary.xlsx`. The certified results for all four voting classes hold up, and Classes 2, 3 and 5 match their ballot-by-ballot schedules exactly. Class 4 does not reconcile: its accepting amount is $63,000 lower in §V.B than in §II.B, and 7 ballots and $827,000 in claims are unaccounted for. None of these discrepancies changes any class result in any scenario I ran.

The workbook has six tabs: Summary, Ballot Detail, Math Checks, Irregularities, Sensitivity, and Notes & Sources. It recalculates with no formula errors, passes validation, and reads back correctly.

**Class results (by number / by dollar amount)**
- **Class 2:** accepts, 90.00% / 94.97%.
- **Class 3:** rejects, 41.67% / 32.36%.
- **Class 4:** accepts, 74.64% / 72.86%. Using the §V.B figure it is 72.81%, which is what the term sheet reports.
- **Class 5:** rejects, 16.67% / 11.35%.

**Math discrepancies (8 of 66 arithmetic checks failed, all in Class 4)**
- **Accepting amount conflict:** §II.B and the narrative say $24,381,400, but the §V.B subtotal and the term sheet say $24,318,400. It looks like a digit transposition, and I can't tell which is right without the full schedule.
- **Unreconciled ballots and claims:** 312 holders, 287 ballots received, 280 counted, 0 excluded, 25 non-voting. That leaves 7 holders and $827,000 of the $38.7M in Class 4 claims unexplained.
- **Term sheet insider figure:** its insider-excluded 72.54% should round to 72.55%. On the §II.B base it is 72.60%.

**Irregularities**
- **Evergreen ballot (Class 2):** the voting agent says the solicitation procedures order doesn't cover a ballot with no box checked. It does: ¶17 says it is counted only if no party objects before the confirmation hearing.
- **Provisional ballots:** ¶24 requires results reported both with and without the 7 provisional ballots. The certification gives only the version that includes them.
- **Insider ballot (Class 4):** Ridgeline Management Holdings LLC (a subsidiary of the debtor) voted $320,000 to accept, per the term sheet, but the certification doesn't disclose it. The term sheet gives it Claim No. 203, which the certification assigns to Larkspur Catering ($520,000). As an intercompany claim it may belong in Class 6, which doesn't vote.
- **Citations and cross-document errors:** the certification cites ¶8 and ¶10 for late and duplicate ballots; the correct paragraphs are ¶14 and ¶¶19–20. It also misdates the designation hearing, misstates the Clearwater address, and calls the Ad Hoc Group second lien when the other documents say first lien.
- **Ballot treatment:** the Garnet Creek designation, Ridgeview late ballot and Magnolia duplicate were each handled correctly.

**Sensitivity:** Class 4 is the only class close to the line. In the combined worst case, its dollar acceptance falls to 69.06% against the 66.67% threshold. It can lose only about $6.2M of accepting claims before failing.

Only 40 of the 281 Class 4 ballot lines are printed in the certification, so Class 4 totals can't be checked ballot by ballot until the voting agent provides the full schedule.

Files are in /workspace/output:
- ballot-tabulation-summary.xlsx
